title: [Practice Tests Plus] - Trends in the Indian fashion and textile industries

parts.title: practice test plus 3 reading test 6 sec 1
parts.passageHtml:
{[During the 1950s, the Indian fashion scene was exciting, stylish and very graceful.][128914]} {[There were no celebrity designers or models, nor were there any labels that were widely recognised.][128928]} {[The value of a garment was judged by its style and fabric rather than by who made it.][128944]} {[It was regarded as perfectly acceptable, even for high-society women, to approach an unknown tailor who could make a garment for a few rupees, providing the perfect fit, finish and style.][128962]} {[They were proud of getting a bargain, and of giving their own name to the end result.][128993]}

{[The 1960s was an era full of mischievousness and celebration in the arts, music and cinema.][129011]} {[The period was characterised by freedom from restrictions and, in the fashion world, an acceptance of innovative types of material such as plastic and coated polyester.][129027]} {[Tight-fitting kurtas(1) and churidars(2) and high coiffures were a trend among women.][129053]}

{[The following decade witnessed an increase in the export of traditional materials, and the arrival in India of international fashion.][129064]} {[Synthetics became trendy, and the disco culture affected the fashion scene.][129085]}

{[It was in the early 80s when the first fashion store ‘Ravissant’ opened in Mumbai.][129098]} {[At that time garments were retailed for a four-figure price tag.][129114]} {[American designers like Calvin Klein became popular.][129125]} {[In India too, contours became more masculine, and even the salwar kameez(3) was designed with shoulder pads.][129133]}

{[With the evolution of designer stores came the culture of designer fashion, along with its hefty price tags.][129152]} {[Whatever a garment was like, consumers were convinced that a higher price tag signified elegant designer fashion, so garments were sold at unbelievable prices.][129171]} {[Meanwhile, designers decided to get themselves noticed by making showy outfits and associating with the right celebrities.][129194]} {[Soon, fashion shows became competitive, each designer attempting to out-do the other in theme, guest list and media coverage.][129212]}

{[In the last decade of the millennium, the market shrank and ethnic wear made a comeback.][129233]} {[During the recession, there was a push to sell at any cost.][129249]} {[With fierce competition the inevitable occurred: the once hefty price tags began their downward journey, and the fashion-show industry followed suit.][129261]} {[However, the liveliness of the Indian fashion scene had not ended - it had merely reached a stable level.][129283]}

{[At the beginning of the 21st century, with new designers and models, and more sensible designs, the fashion industry accelerated once again.][129302]} {[As far as the global fashion industry is concerned, Indian ethnic designs and materials are currently in demand from fashion houses and garment manufacturers.][129325]} {[India is the third largest producer of cotton, the second largest producer of silk, and the fifth largest producer of man-made fibres in the world.][129350]}

{[The Indian garment and fabric industries have many fundamental advantages, in terms of a cheaper, skilled work force, cost-effective production, raw materials, flexibility, and a wide range of designs with sequins, beadwork, and embroidery.][129377]} {[In addition, that India provides garments to international fashion houses at competitive prices, with a shorter lead time, and an effective monopoly on certain designs, is accepted the whole world over.][129410]} {[India has always been regarded as the default source in the embroidered garments segment, but changes in the rate of exchange between the rupee and the dollar has further depressed prices, thereby attracting more buyers.][129440]} {[So the international fashion houses walk away with customised goods, and craftwork is sold at very low rates.][129476]}

{[As far as the fabric market is concerned, the range available in India can attract as well as confuse the buyer.][129496]} {[Much of the production takes place in the small town of Chapa in the eastern state of Bihar, a name one might never have heard of.][129518]} {[Here fabric-making is a family industry; the range and quality of raw silks churned out here belie the crude production methods and equipment.][129544]} {[Surat in Gujarat, is the supplier of an amazing set of jacquards, moss crepes and georgette sheers - all fabrics in high demand.][129567]} {[Another Indian fabric design that has been adopted by the fashion industry is the ‘Madras check’, originally utilised for the universal lungi, a simple lower-body wrap worn in southern India.][129589]} {[This design has now found its way on to bandannas, blouses, home furnishings and almost anything one can think of.][129619]}

{[Ethnic Indian designs with batik and hand-embroidered motifs have also become popular across the world.][129641]} {[Decorative bead work is another product in demand in the international market.][129657]} {[Beads are used to prepare accessory items like belts and bags, and beadwork is now available for haute couture evening wear too.][129670]}

{[(1) knee-length tunics][129693]}

{[(2) trousers][129697]}

{[(3) trouser suit][129701]}

Indian fashion: 1950-2000

1950s

  •    No well-known designers, models or 1
  •    Elegant clothing cost little
  •    Women were pleased to get clothes for a 2 price

1960s

  • New materials, e.g. 3 and polyester
  • Fitted clothing and tall hairstyles

1970s

  • Overseas sales of 4 fabrics rose
  • Influence of international fashion

1980s

  • Opening of fashion store in Mumbai
  • Popularity of American designers
  • Clothing had a 5 shape
  • Designers tried to attract attention by presenting 6 clothes and mixing with stars

1990s

  • Fall in demand for expensive fashion wear
  • Return to 7 clothing

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 8 - 13:

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1

Write:

TRUE          if the statement agrees with the information

FALSE         if the statement contradicts the information

NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

questions.text: At the start of the 21st century, key elements in the Indian fashion industry changed.
questions.explanationHtml:
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight nói là: với nhiều nhà thiết kế và người mẫu mới, các mẫu thiết kế đẹp hơn, ngành thời trang lại "tăng tốc" 1 lần nữa. => và đây là các yếu tố chính của ngành thời trang nói chung.
​
Câu 8: Các yếu tố chính trong ngành thời trang của Ấn Độ thay đổi (ở đây là được đổi mới như ý trong bài) => True.

questions.text: India now exports more than half of the cotton it produces.

Not Given

questions.text: Conditions in India are generally well suited to the manufacture of clothing.
questions.explanationHtml:
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight nói là: ngành may mặc của Ấn Độ có được những lợi thế rất cơ bản,...... (rất nhiều lợi thê, mình không cần hiểu hết ý nghĩa của từng từ để trả lời câu hỏi này nhen các bạn.)
​
Trong câu 10 ý nói: Các điều kiện (conditions) ở Ấn Độ rất là phù hợp với ngành may mặc. => True

questions.text: Indian clothing exports have suffered from changes in the value of its currency.
questions.explanationHtml:
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight nói là: những thay đổi trong tỷ giá giữa "rupee" (đồng tiền của nước Ấn Độ) và "dollar"(US Dollar, đây là đồng tiền được dùng cho các giao dịch Quốc Tế), đã làm giá của các mặt hàng ở Ấn Độ giảm => tắng số lượng người mua=> Tăng lượng xuất khẩu.
​
Câu 11 nói: là việc xuất khẩu hàng may mặc gặp khó khăn vì sự thay đổi tỷ giá. => False.

questions.text: Modern machinery accounts for the high quality of Chapa’s silk.
questions.explanationHtml:
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight nói là: sự đa dạng và chất lượng của tơ tằm thô (raw silks) ở đây làm cho mọi người nghĩ là việc xử lý - sản xuất và máy móc mới những yếu tố làm nên chất lượng lụa của vùng này.
​
Câu 12 nói là: máy móc hiện đại là yếu tố chính tạo nên chất lượng của lụa Chapa. => điều này trái ngược với ý trong bài. => False

questions.text: Some types of Indian craftwork which are internationally popular had humble origins.
questions.explanationHtml:
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight nói là: các mẫu thiết kế dân gian-của các dân tộc thiểu số (ethnic Indian designs) đã trờ nên nổi tiếng khắp thế giới (have become popular across the world).
​
Trong câu 13: Một vài loại hình thủ công (craftwork) mà đang được nổi tiếng cả thế giới, thì có 1 xuất phát điểm rất là giản dị (humble origins) =>Đúng với ý trong bài => True
